damage.title: Extent of the damage
damage.summary: The British report found that the damage extended over a length of about 300 ft on the starboard side, about 10 ft above the keel, and opened six compartments: the forepeak, Nos. 1, 2 and 3 holds and Nos. 6 and 5 boiler rooms.
damage.note: "The damage extended over a length of about 300 ft." (Extent of the Damage). The wording is established; the figure is the court's estimate.

alternatives.position: About 200 ft, from the peak tank to just abaft bulkhead E; the transcript also prints "about 500 feet", marked as an error by Halpern.

damage.title: Total area open to the sea
damage.summary: Edward Wilding of Harland and Wolff estimated before the British Inquiry that the openings amounted to "somewhere about 12 square feet" in all, and believed they were a series of separate punctures, not one continuous tear.
damage.note: Wilding, Day 19, Q20422–20425, back-calculated from about 16,000 tons of water in about 40 minutes under a head of about 25 ft. In 1915 he gave a band of 9 to 15 square feet; Halpern's re-derivation gives 11.67.

damage.title: Sonar survey of the buried bow (1996)
damage.summary: A sub-bottom sonar survey reported six thin openings spread over six compartments, totalling about 12 to 13 square feet.
damage.note: Reported in the press in 1997; the lengths and positions of the individual openings were not found in the sources read.

damage.title: Collision simulation (2025)
damage.summary: A simulation presented with the 2022 scan of the wreck, led by Jeom-Kee Paik, describes a glancing blow leaving a line of small punctures along a narrow strip of hull across six compartments. The damaged area itself is buried in sediment and is not visible on the scan.
damage.note: Reported by the press from a documentary; no peer-reviewed publication was found.

damage.title: Initial rate of flooding
damage.summary: About 13.3 long tons of water per second at first, falling as the levels inside rose; about 6.7 long tons per second on average over the first forty minutes.
damage.note: Halpern's falling-head model for 11.67 square feet under 25 ft of head; the average follows from Wilding's 16,000 tons in 40 minutes.

damage.title: Pumping capacity
damage.summary: The ballast and bilge pumps could together discharge about 1,700 tons an hour, which the British report judged could not possibly have coped with the inflow.
damage.note: Five pumps of 250 tons an hour and three of 150 (report, Machinery); the total is their sum.

damage.title: What the subdivision could withstand
damage.summary: The ship was designed to float with any two adjoining compartments flooded and could have survived the flooding of the first four. The first five could not be lost.
damage.note: Report, Structure and Observations; Wilding, Q20286–20364.

levels.note: Probably full to the top of bulkhead E, at E-deck level, about one hour after the collision (report).

levels.note: Only the forward starboard bunker was open to the sea, through a hole about two feet abaft bulkhead E; the inflow, likened to a fire hose, was held by the pumps.
Stokehold still workable until a rush of water came through the pass between the boilers (Barrett). Halpern follows Barrett's estimate of about 1:10.

alternatives.position: The bunker door gave way about an hour after the collision, about 12:40.

compartments.note: No level was recorded after the room was abandoned. The twenty minutes allowed for it to fill are the project's assumption; the cause of the rush of water (bunker door or bulkhead) is itself disputed.
